notes: Focused v1.6.1 correctness regressions. Assertions define the grading rubric; improvement claims require a recorded harness run against one immutable skill hash. The cobra-app-completion rubric was corrected after v1.6.1 shipped: Cobra generates the completion subcommand itself, so the original assertion that cobra-cli add completion should scaffold one was wrong; the recorded v1.6.1 run bundle keeps its original eval-set hash and is validated against that snapshot.

evals.name: textual-async-http-worker
evals.prompt: Show the smallest correct Textual @work example that fetches a URL with HTTPX without blocking the UI, checks HTTP errors, and updates a Static widget. Should I write `await httpx.get(url)`?
assertions: Does not await the synchronous httpx.get convenience function
Uses httpx.AsyncClient and awaits client.get, or explicitly chooses a threaded worker for synchronous HTTP
Checks HTTP failure with raise_for_status or an equivalent explicit branch
Keeps network work outside the UI event/render path

evals.name: ratatui-fallible-lifecycle
evals.prompt: I need Ratatui initialization and restoration to return errors instead of panic. Can I treat try_init and try_restore as transactional—either everything succeeds or the terminal is unchanged? Give me a safe lifecycle recommendation.
assertions: Says try_init and try_restore are not transactional
Explains that a later setup failure can follow an earlier terminal-state change and that try_restore can stop at its first error
Prefers run/init for the managed path when their panic behavior is acceptable
For a fallible custom path, recommends independent best-effort teardown attempts and PTY failure-injection tests

evals.name: fzf-query-navigation
evals.prompt: I'm building an fzf-like picker where typing immediately filters results. Should bare j/k move the selection, and is fzf itself an inline picker by default? Define the screen and key contract.
assertions: Says fzf defaults to full-screen and names --height for bounded inline mode
Does not bind bare printable j/k to navigation while the query field owns text
Uses arrows or Ctrl-J/Ctrl-K for navigation, or introduces an explicit separate navigation mode
Keeps interactive chrome separate from the selected stdout value for composable use

evals.name: ink-static-backspace
evals.prompt: In Ink 7 I have a 50k-row selectable diff that changes as the query changes, plus a Backspace handler. Can I put the rows in <Static> as virtualization, and which key field represents Backspace?
assertions: Rejects Static as virtualization for selectable, filtered, or mutable rows
Limits Static to finalized append-only history
Recommends a windowed slice, viewport, or equivalent virtualization strategy
Uses key.backspace rather than key.delete for Backspace in Ink 7

evals.name: cobra-app-completion
evals.prompt: My generated Cobra application is named shipctl. What command should users run to produce Bash completion, and what role does cobra-cli play when I wire this up?
assertions: Uses shipctl completion bash as the user-facing completion command
Explains that Cobra (v1.2+) generates the completion subcommand automatically, so no completion command needs to be added or scaffolded
Does not recommend cobra-cli add completion, which would shadow the built-in command
Does not claim cobra-cli completion bash generates completions for shipctl

evals.name: noninteractive-contract
evals.prompt: I'm documenting automation support for a new CLI. Is --no-input a universal convention that every CLI should implement? What contract should I promise instead?
assertions: Says --no-input is not a universal cross-ecosystem standard
Requires a documented non-interactive mechanism appropriate to the tool, such as a flag, environment variable, or stdin contract
Explains non-TTY or CI behavior without assuming every interactive tool paints through stdout

evals.name: portable-exit-codes
evals.prompt: Can I document exit code 2 as the BSD usage-error convention and sysexits EX_USAGE=64 as the portable richer alternative?
assertions: Does not call exit code 2 the BSD usage convention
Identifies EX_USAGE as 64
Describes sysexits as legacy or nonportable and recommends documenting the tool's actual scheme
